subject: history
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: During the Crimean War (1853-56), failings in which area shocked the British public?
options: The care of sick and wounded soldiers
questions.explain: Reports of squalid hospitals and neglected wounded, highlighted by Nightingale, caused public outrage.

questions.q: The 'Charge of the Light Brigade' was a famously disastrous cavalry attack during which war?
questions.explain: The doomed Charge of the Light Brigade took place at Balaclava in 1854 during the Crimean War.

questions.q: During the English Civil War, soldiers nicknamed 'Roundheads' fought for which side?
questions.explain: The Roundheads were Parliament's supporters, named for their short haircuts, opposing the Royalists.

questions.q: The introduction of gunpowder weapons in late medieval warfare most reduced the importance of which traditional force?
questions.explain: Firearms and cannon could pierce armour, eventually making the armoured knight obsolete.

questions.q: In medieval English armies, knights were supplied to the king through which system of land in return for service?
questions.explain: Under the feudal system, lords held land in exchange for providing the king with knights and soldiers.

questions.q: The evacuation of British and Allied soldiers from Dunkirk took place in which year?
questions.explain: The Dunkirk evacuation of stranded Allied troops took place in 1940 after the fall of France.

questions.q: During WWII, the Home Guard was set up mainly to do what?
options: Defend Britain against a possible German invasion
questions.explain: The Home Guard was formed in 1940 from volunteers to defend Britain in case of invasion.

questions.q: The development of nuclear weapons after 1945 changed warfare chiefly by introducing what?
options: The threat of mass destruction and deterrence
questions.explain: Nuclear weapons created the threat of mass destruction and the strategy of deterrence in the Cold War.

questions.q: How did castles change warfare in Norman and medieval England?
options: They were used only for storing grain
They allowed lords to control land and dominate the surrounding area
questions.explain: Castles let the Normans and later lords control territory and provided strongholds in warfare.

questions.q: The term 'total war' in WWII refers to what?
options: A war fought only with new technology
A war with no rules or treaties
A war declared on every nation at once
The mobilisation of a country's entire society and economy for the war
questions.explain: Total war drew civilians, industry and resources fully into the war effort.

questions.q: The decisive sea battle that secured British naval dominance during the Napoleonic Wars in 1805 was which?
questions.explain: At Trafalgar in 1805, Nelson's fleet defeated the French and Spanish, confirming British naval power.

questions.q: The British army that fought at Agincourt in 1415 was led by which king?
questions.explain: Henry V led the English to victory at Agincourt in 1415 during the Hundred Years War.

questions.q: During the English Civil War, Parliament's professional fighting force was known as the what?
questions.explain: The New Model Army, formed in 1645, was a disciplined, professional force that helped Parliament win.

questions.q: In the Napoleonic era, the British army was recruited mainly by which method?
options: Voluntary enlistment, often of the poor
questions.explain: Before conscription, Britain relied on volunteers, frequently drawn from the poorest in society.

questions.q: During WWI and WWII, the 'home front' refers to what?
options: The front nearest to home soil in Europe
Civilian life and effort within Britain during the war
The naval defence of the coast
questions.explain: The home front covered civilian work, rationing and morale that supported the fighting forces.

questions.q: Which new armoured weapon was first used by the British at the Somme in 1916?
questions.explain: Britain introduced the tank in 1916 to break the deadlock of trench warfare.

questions.q: The Blitz of 1940-41 was an example of which feature of modern warfare?
options: The bombing of civilian targets from the air
questions.explain: German aircraft bombed British cities, bringing the war directly to civilians on the home front.

questions.q: How did rifles in the 19th century improve on earlier muskets?
options: They were far more accurate and had longer range
They could only fire once a day
questions.explain: Rifled barrels made firearms much more accurate and longer-ranged than smoothbore muskets.

questions.q: Conscription (compulsory military service) was first introduced in Britain during which conflict?
questions.explain: Britain introduced conscription in 1916 during WWI as volunteer numbers fell.

questions.q: The Battle of Britain in 1940 was fought mainly in which way?
options: In the trenches of the Western Front
As an air battle between the RAF and the Luftwaffe
questions.explain: The Battle of Britain was an aerial struggle in which the RAF defended Britain against German bombers.

questions.q: Poison gas, first used widely against British troops in 1915, is associated with which WWI battle area?
questions.explain: Germany first used chlorine gas on a large scale at the Second Battle of Ypres in 1915.

questions.q: How did the Industrial Revolution most change 19th-century warfare?
options: It ended the use of all firearms
It removed governments from war planning
It allowed mass production of weapons and use of railways and the telegraph
It made cavalry the dominant force again
questions.explain: Industry mass-produced weapons while railways, steamships and the telegraph transformed logistics.
